children: said Tuesday it reached a positive final investment decision to build the $1.6B, 215-mile South Mississippi pipeline project, which will aim to give shippers greater access to natural gas from multiple basins across the southeast U.S. when it enters service, projected in 2030.
said it has secured long-term, demand-based transportation agreements to support the construction of a 36-inch pipeline with a capacity of 1.2 Bcf/day.

The partnership said it expects to operate the project and own 51%, with the remaining ownership coming from shippers, and is holding a binding open season for additional customer commitments to the project, which is set to end November 25.

also said it completed the addition of equipment to boost gas flows on its Rover pipeline system in the Midwest, with the 250K MMBtu/day expansion of firm transportation commitments coming online November 1, and it executed two agreements to provide 150K MMBtu/day of natural gas transportation service from its MRT pipeline to two power plants under construction in Missouri.

while raising its full-year guidance above analyst estimates.

The partnership said it now expects FY 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $19.7B-$19.9B, compared to its previous range of $18.8B-$19.1B, and anticipates $5.4B-$5.6B in growth capital spending for 2026 and ~$7B for 2027.

title: Energy Transfer approves $1.6B South Mississippi pipeline project
